title: Continuous Feedback Processing
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 21 participants performing a continuous feedback prediction task in which they learned to predict the final level of an animated rising bar based on probabilistic cues. Participants made predictions using mouse responses and received point-based feedback, with trial difficulty manipulated through six gnome cue conditions varying in outcome predictability. The dataset includes behavioral responses, timing information, and neural recordings suitable for investigating feedback processing and predictive learning mechanisms.
methods_description: Participants completed a prediction task where each trial consisted of a fixation cross (400-600 ms), a gnome cue (1500 ms) indicating trial type, a bar outline (until response), bar animation (1 degree per second), and final outcome display (1000 ms). Six conditions manipulated outcome predictability: two highly predictable conditions (consistently low or high), two somewhat predictable conditions (80% biased), and two unpredictable conditions (equal probability or random uniform distribution). Participant responses were recorded via mouse input, and trial events were marked with trigger codes indicating fixation, cue onset, bar appearance, response, animation start, and animation end.
